questions.question: A sum of Rs. 10500 becomes Rs. 17745 in 2 years at the rate of compound interest. If the interest is compounded annually, then what will be the rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 10500 becomes Rs. 17745 in 2 years at the rate of compound interest. If the interest is compounded annually, then what will be the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Amount = Principal × [1 + r/100]n

17745 = 10500 × [1 + r/100]2

⇒ 17745/10500 = [1 + r/100]2

⇒ 169/100 = [1 + r/100]2

Taking square root on both sides, we get,

⇒ 13/10 = 1 + r/100
⇒ 13/10 = (100 + r)/100
⇒ 13 = (100 + r)10
⇒ 130 = 100 + r
⇒ r = 130 –100
⇒ r = 30

∴ Rate = 0.30 × 100 = 30%

questions.question: A person invests Rs. 8192 at 15% compounded after every 5 months for \(1{{1} \over 4}\) years. Then find the compound interest.
questions.questionHtml: A person invests Rs. 8192 at 15% compounded after every 5 months for \(1{{1} \over 4}\) years. Then find the compound interest.
questions.solution:
Given 

A person invests = Rs. 8192 

Rate of Interest = 15% = (15/12) × 5 = 6.25%

Time = 5/4 years = 15 months 

Formula Used 

Amount = Principal(1 + R/100)t (where t = no. of times)

Calculation 

No. of times = 15/5 = 3

Amount = 8192(1 + 6.25/100)3

⇒ 9826

Compound Interest = Amount - Principal = 9,826 - 8192 = Rs. 1,634

∴ The required answer is Rs. 1634

questions.question: A sum of money becomes Rs. 32490 in 2 years when kept at compound interest (compounded annually). If the rate of interest is 14 percent per annum, then what is the sum of money?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money becomes Rs. 32490 in 2 years when kept at compound interest (compounded annually). If the rate of interest is 14 percent per annum, then what is the sum of money?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rate 14% = 7/50. Compounding factor = 57/50.

For 2 years, the ratio of Principal (P) to Amount (A) is (50)2 : (57)2 = 2500 : 3249.

Given Amount = 3249 units = ₹32490.

→ 1 unit = ₹10.

Principal (Sum) = 2500 units × 10 = ₹25000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹25000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Amount (A) = ₹32490

Rate of interest (R) = 14% p.a.

Time period (n) = 2 years

Formula Used:

The formula for Compound Interest is: A = P(1 + R/100)n

Calculations:

⇒ 32490 = P(1 + 14/100)2

⇒ 32490 = P(114/100)2

⇒ 32490 = P(57/50)2

⇒ 32490 = P × (3249 / 2500)

⇒ P = (32490 × 2500) / 3249

⇒ P = 10 × 2500

⇒ P = 25000

∴ The correct answer is ₹25000.

Additional Information

Effective Interest Rate

For two years at R%, the effective Compound Interest rate is R + R + (R×R)/100. In this case: 14 + 14 + 1.96 = 29.96%.

CI and SI Difference

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is calculated as: D = P × (R/100)2.

Compounding Frequency

If compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time is doubled (2n) in the formula.

questions.question: Narender borrowed Rs.25,000 for one year at 20% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly, then find the interest paid by Narender.
questions.questionHtml: Narender borrowed Rs.25,000 for one year at 20% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly, then find the interest paid by Narender.
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs.25,000

Time = 1 year

Rate = 20%

Condition = half yearly

Concept used:

If the interest is calculated half yearly, then

New rate = Rate/2

New time = Time × 2

Formulae used:

Compound interest = P × (1 + R/100)T – P

Calculations:

If the interest is calculated half yearly, then

New rate = Rate/2 = 20/2 = 10%

New time = Time × 2 = 1 × 2 = 2

Compound interest = P × (1 + R/100)T – P

⇒ 25,000 × (1 + 10/100)2 – 25,000

⇒ 25,000 × (110/100)2 – 25,000

⇒ 25,000 × {(11/10) × (11/10) – 1}

⇒ 25,000 × (121 – 100)/100

⇒ 25,0 × 21 = 5250

∴ The interest paid by Narender is Rs.5250.

Smart Trick

Rate = 20/2 = 10%

Effective rate = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%

Compound interest = 21% of 25000 = 5250

∴ The interest paid by Narender is Rs.5250.

questions.question: A certain sum becomes 1.96 times in two years at CI then what will be the rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum becomes 1.96 times in two years at CI then what will be the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Amount (A) to Principal (P) for 2 years = 1.96 : 1 = 196 : 100.

For 1 year, take the square root: √196 : √100 = 14 : 10.

Interest earned in 1 year = 14 − 10 = 4 units on a base of 10.

Rate of Interest = (4 ÷ 10) × 100 = 40%.

∴ The correct answer is 40%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time (n) = 2 years

Amount (A) = 1.96 × Principal (P)

Formula Used:

A = P(1 + R/100)n

Calculations:

⇒ 1.96P = P(1 + R/100)2

⇒ 1.96 = (1 + R/100)2

⇒ √1.96 = 1 + R/100

⇒ 1.4 = 1 + R/100

⇒ R/100 = 1.4 − 1

⇒ R/100 = 0.4

⇒ R = 0.4 × 100

⇒ R = 40%

∴ The correct answer is 40%.

Additional Information

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For a period of 2 years at R%, the net effective rate is calculated as (R + R + (R × R)/100)%.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is P(R/100)2.

Compound Interest Formula

The total amount A after n years is given by A = P(1 + r/k)nk, where k is the number of times interest is compounded per year.

questions.question: A sum becomes 27 times in 3 years, compounded annually at a certain rate of interest. Calculate annual interest rate.
questions.questionHtml: A sum becomes 27 times in 3 years, compounded annually at a certain rate of interest. Calculate annual interest rate.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For compounded annually growth, use the root of the times-factor based on the time period.

Growth factor for 3 years = 27 times.

Annual growth factor = 3√27 = 3.

Rate (R) = (Annual Factor − 1) × 100% = (3 − 1) × 100% = 200%.

∴ The correct answer is 200%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = P

Amount (A) = 27P

Time (t) = 3 years

Formula Used:

A = P(1 + R/100)t

⇒ 27P = P(1 + R/100)3

⇒ 27 = (1 + R/100)3

⇒ (3)3 = (1 + R/100)3

⇒ 3 = 1 + R/100

⇒ R/100 = 3 − 1

⇒ R/100 = 2

⇒ R = 200%

∴ The correct answer is 200%.

Additional Information

Effective Interest Rate

When interest is compounded more than once a year, the actual rate earned is Reff = [1 + (r/n)]n − 1, where 'n' is the number of compounding periods.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is CI − SI = P(R/100)2.

Rule of 72

A quick shortcut to estimate the doubling time of an investment: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate of Interest.

questions.question: A sum of amount to Rs. 3,025 in 3 year and to Rs. 4,225 in 5 year at a certain rate percent per annum, when the interest is compound yearly. find the rate of interest.
questions.questionHtml: A sum of amount to Rs. 3,025 in 3 year and to Rs. 4,225 in 5 year at a certain rate percent per annum, when the interest is compound yearly. find the rate of interest.
questions.solution:
Given:

Sum of amount in 3 year = Rs. 3,025

Sum of amount in 5 year = Rs. 4,225

Formula used:

Amount at CI = P(1 + r/100)t

where P = Principle, r = rate per annum, and t = time

Calculation:

For 3 year,

3025 = P(1 + r/100)3      ------- (1)

For 5 year,

4225 = P(1 + r/100)5      ------- (2)

Dividing equation (2) from equation (1)

4225/3025 = P(1 + r/100)5 ÷ P(1 + r/100)3 

⇒ 169/121 = (1 + r/100)2

⇒ 1 + r/100 = \(\sqrt{\frac{169}{121}}\)

⇒ r/100 = 13/11 - 1

⇒ r/100 = 2/11

⇒ r = 200/11

⇒ r = 18\(2 \over 11\)%

∴ Rate of interest is 18\(2 \over 11\)%.

questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interests on Rs. 25000 for 1 year at 6% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly? (In Rs.)
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference between the compound interests on Rs. 25000 for 1 year at 6% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly? (In Rs.)
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal(P) = Rs. 25000

Time period(T) = 1 yr

Rate of interest(R) = 6%

Formula used:

C.I1 = \(P× \bigg(1+\dfrac{R}{200} \bigg)^{2t}\)- P (for compounded half-yearly)

C.I2 = \(P× \bigg(1+\dfrac{R}{100} \bigg)^t\)- P (for compounded yearly)

Calculation:

C.I1 = \(25000× \bigg(1+ \dfrac{6}{200} \bigg)^2 - 25000 \) 

⇒ \(25000× \bigg(\dfrac{103}{100} \bigg)^2 - 25000\) 

⇒ 26522.5 - 25000 = Rs. 1522.5

C.I2 = \(25000× \bigg(1+ \dfrac{6}{100} \bigg)\) - 25000

⇒ 25000 × \(106\over100\) - 25000

⇒ 26500 - 25000 = Rs. 1500 

Difference between compound interests compounded half-yearly and yearly = 1522.5 - 1500 = Rs. 22.5.

∴ The answer is Rs. 22.5.

Shortcut TrickRate = 6% when compounded yearly, 

At this rate time = 1

Rate = 6/2 = 3% when compounded half-yearly, 

At this rate time = 2

Calculation:

Using the tree method,

For yearly,

⇒ CI for 1 year is 1500 when compounded yearly,

For half-yearly, 

 

⇒ CI for 1 year = 750 + 750 + 22.5 = 1522.5 when compounded half-yearly,

Now the difference, 

⇒ 1522.5 - 1500 = 22.5

∴ The answer is Rs. 22.5.

questions.question: What is the compound interest on Rs. 5000 in 3 years, if the rate of interest is 4% for the first year, 3% for the second year and 2% for the third year?
questions.questionHtml: What is the compound interest on Rs. 5000 in 3 years, if the rate of interest is 4% for the first year, 3% for the second year and 2% for the third year?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply Successive Percentage increase on the Principal of ₹5000.

Year 1: 5000 + 4% of 5000 = 5000 + 200 = ₹5200

Year 2: 5200 + 3% of 5200 = 5200 + 156 = ₹5356

Year 3: 5356 + 2% of 5356 = 5356 + 107.12 = ₹5463.12

Compound Interest = Final Amount − Initial Principal = 5463.12 − 5000 = ₹463.12

∴ The correct answer is ₹463.12.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹5000

Rates of Interest: R1 = 4%, R2 = 3%, R3 = 2%

Time (n) = 3 years

Formula Used:

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R1/100) × (1 + R2/100) × (1 + R3/100)

Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

Calculations:

⇒ A = 5000 × (1 + 4/100) × (1 + 3/100) × (1 + 2/100)

⇒ A = 5000 × (104/100) × (103/100) × (102/100)

⇒ A = 5000 × 1.04 × 1.03 × 1.02

⇒ A = 5200 × 1.03 × 1.02

⇒ A = 5356 × 1.02

⇒ A = ₹5463.12

⇒ CI = 5463.12 − 5000

⇒ CI = ₹463.12

∴ The correct answer is ₹463.12.

Additional Information

Effective Rate of Interest

For two years with different rates a and b, the effective rate is [a + b + (a × b)/100]%.

CI vs SI Difference (2 Years)

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is P × (R/100)2.

Compounding Frequency

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time is doubled (2n).
